fact: The Ministry of ICT permanent secretary says Uganda is still developing a dedicated AI legal framework but existing laws already apply, and election misconduct is unlawful online, with misuse of AI to mislead carrying consequences.
The MoICT/ITU assessment lists a lack of AI policy, legal and regulatory framework among its major findings.

Uganda Communications Commission Executive Director Nyombi Thembo, speaking on AI-generated deepfakes and disinformation, said the Computer Misuse (Amendment) Act 2022 is in full effect, with up to 7 years' imprisonment or a Shs10 million fine for hate speech, cyber stalking and malicious information.

UNESCO's account says participants at the 26 May 2026 consultation expressed concern about the absence of existing binding mechanisms to monitor AI-related harms in Uganda, particularly in gender and health.
NITA-U's Julian Rweju said the Bank of Uganda has recently rolled out specific regulations to support and govern AI within the financial sector.
